payload.summary: Five parallel analyses (completeness, consistency, feasibility, testability, security/perf) surfaced 3 critical, 12 high, and ~12 medium findings; all at or above medium were fixed. The largest: the opt-in unit contradicted itself across four documents — resolved by new D13 (forward opt-in per contract document, reverse opt-in per capability via a traceability-exclusions.yaml that is simultaneously the requirement-exclusion home D4 was missing). Change scope, slug algorithm, concentration trigger, and malformed-input behavior are now deterministic; a skill-workflow delta, task 2.0 (schema extension/promotion), task 4.2b (flagship reverse opt-in), and wp-matrix/wp-wiring packages were added; phase 3 renumbered to 3.1-3.16.
completed_work: F1/F2/F7 (critical/high): directional opt-in split (D13), traceability-exclusions.schema.json added, mixed-capability + reverse opt-in scenarios, task 4.2b authored, 5.2 scoped forward-only
F3 (critical): touched-set definition for both directions, --change required, merge base pinned and fail-closed, change-scoped reverse + unresolvable-scope scenarios
F4: task 2.0 (extend cli-contract.schema.json, promote both schemas) with wp-model write_allow widened to the schema paths

F5/F6/F9/F10/F11/F17/F18/F19: valid-exclusion suppression, cross-capability reverse credit + unresolvable case, RENAMED handling, one-or-more wording, deterministic concentration (capability denominator), normative slug algorithm + collision fail-closed, malformed-input requirement (4 scenarios), pinned canonical output lines
F8: sweep blocking semantics specced (new requirement, 2 scenarios); proposal wording fixed both places; push-triggered naming unified
F12: specs/skill-workflow/spec.md delta (MODIFIED 3-Phase Incremental Generation, ADDED Validation-Time Requirement Traceability Gate)
F13: archetype-only model constraint written into task 2.2 and wp-model (replaces the gatekeeper's incorrect write_allow fix)

Validation: openspec validate --strict PASS; validate_work_packages.py VALID (schema, depends_on, DAG, lock keys)

decisions.title: D13: one opt-in switch per direction; the exclusions file is the reverse switch
decisions.rationale: Three analysts independently found the opt-in unit contradictory (per contract vs per capability vs per file), and the per-capability reading made task 5.2's staging infeasible (122 requirements to triage before locks.yaml could opt in). Forward and reverse are different claims with different owners; keying reverse on the exclusions file means the switch cannot be flipped without doing the triage it certifies, and it gives requirement-side exclusions the home the schema lacked.

decisions.title: Reject the gatekeeper's proposed wp-model write_allow widening
decisions.rationale: Deeper analysis showed interface-descriptor.schema.json is only reachable from InterfaceDescriptor; the traceability field belongs on archetype-only models with an absent default, keeping both CI byte-identity gates green with no new write scope. The real gap was that this constraint was written nowhere — it is now task 2.2's note and wp-model's description.

decisions.title: Add a skill-workflow spec delta rather than leaving skill wiring unspecced
decisions.rationale: skill-workflow already specs Contract Ref hand-population and (per the ri-08 precedent) is where workflow-blocking gates are specced; changing that behavior without a delta would be exactly the unspecced-surface problem this change attacks. Kept minimal: one MODIFIED requirement, one ADDED. The ordinal Req ID scheme is deliberately not changed; the generator joins by parse position.

decisions.title: Fail-closed scope inputs for the change-scoped gate
decisions.rationale: An unresolvable merge base or missing change id must error, never resolve to an empty touched set — a blocking gate that evaluates nothing while exiting zero is the defect class the change exists to eliminate, and this repo has already been bitten by the shallow-clone variant.

decisions.title: Skip vendor review inside this skill run
decisions.rationale: The autopilot orchestrator runs PLAN_REVIEW (multi-vendor parallel-review-plan) immediately after PLAN_ITERATE; dispatching the same review twice doubles cost for no information. Stated openly per the no-silent-fallback rule.
